subject.title: feat(tui): opt-in persistence and agent visibility for `!`/`!!` local shell commands

question: Should OpenClaw permanently allow explicitly approved TUI-local shell output to be stored in session history and optionally exposed to the agent through an operator-admin gateway contract?
rationale: Mechanical defects can be repaired, but tests cannot authorize the durable sensitive-data boundary, the `!`/`!!` convention, or the long-term privileged protocol surface.

options.title: Approve identity-scoped opt-in
options.body: Adopt the capability with local-only as the default after the defects, conflicts, and real-path proof are resolved.

options.title: Keep output local
options.body: Retain local shell execution without durable transcript storage or model visibility.

options.title: Use a generic share action
options.body: Share selected local output through an explicit generic transcript interaction instead of persistent `!` and `!!` semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve identity-scoped opt-in
recommendation.body: Adopt the capability with local-only as the default after the defects, conflicts, and real-path proof are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history covers the existing TUI consent UX and the gateway, transcript, and protocol decision surfaces affected by this choice.
